files.purpose: Implements the agent question flow at the end of a thread: a ChatBadge row reading '1 question' / 'N questions' with caption 'to answer', and the paged QuestionSheet popover that collects per-question choice picks plus free text and hands them back to ThreadRuntime.answer. Also contains the private QuestionPage row renderer and the private QuestionAnswers collection/counting helper.
key_symbols: QuestionBadgeRow (struct View; let request: QuestionRequest, let runtime: ThreadRuntime, @State isShowingQuestions)
QuestionSheet.pageHeight (private let CGFloat, computed in init)
calls_into: QuestionRequest, QuestionRequest.Question (id, header, prompt, choices, allowsMultiple, allowsOther, isSecret), QuestionRequest.Choice (label, detail) from DroppyCode/Core/Models/Requests.swift
Chrome.accent, Chrome.overlay(_:), Chrome.primaryText, Chrome.secondaryText, Chrome.panelSlide, Chrome.hover
SwiftUI ScrollView, SecureField, TextField, Capsule, RoundedRectangle, Divider, Button
state_owned: QuestionBadgeRow.@State isShowingQuestions: Bool = false (drives the ChatBadge isPresented binding)
QuestionSheet.@State selections: [String: [String]] (question.id -> picked choice labels; seeded in init with recommended labels)
QuestionSheet.@State written: [String: String] = [:] (question.id -> free text / secret text)
QuestionSheet.@State page: Int = 0 (current question page index)
side_effects: runtime.answer(request, answers:) sends the answers back to the agent runtime
closePopover?() dismisses the badge popover before answering
Task { @MainActor } with Task.sleep(for: .seconds(delay)) drives the 0.18 s auto-advance after a single-choice pick
init() constructs an NSHostingView per question purely to measure fittingSize (synchronous AppKit layout during view init)
platform_assumptions: AppKit NSHostingView(rootView:).fittingSize used at init time to measure SwiftUI content height (macOS only API)
NSPopover-backed badge detail presentation that freezes its content size at open time, which is why the height is premeasured
SF Symbols names: questionmark.bubble, chevron.left, checkmark.square.fill, square, checkmark.circle.fill, circle
macOS control styles: .bordered, .borderedProminent, .roundedBorder text field style, controlSize(.regular)
keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction) mapping Return to the prominent button
ui_elements: Badge title: '1 question' when count == 1, otherwise '\(count) questions'; caption 'to answer'; needsAttention: true; glyph Image(systemName: "questionmark.bubble").foregroundStyle(.tint)
Sheet fixed width 460; page viewport height = min(max(tallest measured page, 120), 360)

Page indicator (only when count > 1): HStack spacing 5 of Capsule buttons, active capsule 18x6, inactive 6x6; fill = Chrome.accent when current, Chrome.accent.opacity(0.35) when answered, Chrome.overlay(0.18) otherwise
Page counter text: verbatim '\(page + 1) of \(count)', font .system(size: 11), monospacedDigit, Chrome.secondaryText
Indicator row padding: .horizontal 16, .top 12, .bottom 6; animation Chrome.panelSlide on page

Pages laid out in one HStack(spacing: 0), each a ScrollView(.vertical) with frame width 460 height pageHeight; the row uses .offset(x: -CGFloat(page) * 460), .clipped(), animated with Chrome.panelSlide
Divider between the pages and the footer
Footer HStack spacing 8, controlSize(.regular), padding .horizontal 16 / .vertical 10
Back button (count > 1): Image(systemName: "chevron.left"), .bordered, disabled when page == 0, help 'Previous question'
Remaining counter text: '1 question still to answer' or '\(unanswered) questions still to answer', font .system(size: 11), .secondary, lineLimit(1)
Button 'Skip' (.bordered), help 'Sends no answers and lets the agent carry on'
Button 'Next' (.borderedProminent + keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)) while page < count-1 and not complete; otherwise 'Next' as .bordered plus 'Send' as .borderedProminent with .defaultAction
'Next' help text 'Goes to the next question'
'Send' help text 'Sends your answers' when complete, else 'Answer the question to send' (count == 1) or 'Answer all \(count) questions to send'
QuestionPage: VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10), padding .horizontal 16 / .vertical 12
Question header: uppercase (textCase(.uppercase)), font .system(size: 11, weight: .medium), Chrome.secondaryText, shown only when non-empty
Question prompt: font .system(size: 13, weight: .semibold), Chrome.primaryText, fixedSize vertical, textSelection(.enabled)
Choice row: HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 10); symbol font .system(size: 14), frame width 18, padding .top 1, tinted Chrome.accent when selected else Chrome.secondaryText
Choice label font .system(size: 13, weight: .semibold when selected else .regular), Chrome.primaryText
'Recommended' pill: Text("Recommended"), font .system(size: 10, weight: .medium), Chrome.accent, padding .horizontal 6 / .vertical 2, background Capsule fill Chrome.accent.opacity(0.14)
Choice detail: font .system(size: 11), Chrome.secondaryText, fixedSize vertical; inner VStack spacing 2, label HStack spacing 6

Choice row chrome: padding .horizontal 12 / .vertical 9, background RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 10, style: .continuous) filled Chrome.accent.opacity(0.12) when selected else Chrome.overlay(0.06), contentShape(.rect), .buttonStyle(.plain), animation Chrome.hover on isSelected

Free-text field placeholders: SecureField 'Your answer' when question.isSecret; TextField 'Your answer' when there are no choices, otherwise 'Something else'; .roundedBorder, controlSize(.regular), onSubmit -> advance()
feature_notes: Choices whose label contains 'recommended' (case-insensitive) are preselected: all matches for a multiple-choice question, only the first match for a single-choice question

A trailing ' (Recommended)' suffix is stripped from the displayed label (case-insensitive suffix compare) and shown instead as a separate 'Recommended' pill; a label that merely contains 'recommended' elsewhere still gets the pill but keeps its full text
Picking a choice on a single-choice question that is not the last page auto-advances after 0.18 seconds
Tapping a selected single-choice option clears the selection (current = isSelected ? [] : [choice.label]); multiple-choice toggles membership and appends new picks in tap order
Choices are ForEach-keyed by enumerated offset so two identically worded choices both remain tappable
The free-text field appears when question.allowsOther is true or the question has no choices at all
Answers per question = picked labels plus, if non-empty after trimming .whitespacesAndNewlines, the written text appended as an extra value
unansweredCount counts questions whose collected answer array is empty; Send is disabled until it reaches 0
'Skip' sends an empty dictionary [:] as the answers, which lets the agent carry on
Return (defaultAction) is bound to Next while an answer is still missing and a later page exists; once everything is answered Return sends from any page
advance() on the last page sends automatically when nothing is unanswered, otherwise does nothing
send() closes the popover first, then calls runtime.answer, so the popover animates away from the badge rather than being torn down with it
The tallest page is measured once in init via NSHostingView at width 460 and the height is clamped into [120, 360]; nothing afterwards changes the sheet size
Tapping a page-indicator capsule jumps directly to that question, animated with Chrome.panelSlide
unresolved_questions: The exact values of Chrome.panelSlide, Chrome.hover, Chrome.accent, Chrome.overlay(_:), Chrome.primaryText and Chrome.secondaryText are defined in the UI/Chrome layer and were not read in this bundle
QuestionRequest / QuestionRequest.Question field semantics (for example whether isSecret also forbids choices) come from DroppyCode/Core/Models/Requests.swift, not read here

How ThreadRuntime.answer treats an empty answers dictionary versus a dictionary of empty arrays (the Skip path sends [:], the Send path sends an entry per question id) is decided in ThreadRuntime.swift
The precise popover size-freezing behavior of BadgePopoverCoordinator and the closePopover environment key is in UI/Chrome/Popovers.swift, not read here

files.purpose: Defines ApprovalCard, the glass card shown for a pending ApprovalRequest: warning-tinted symbol and headline, a kind-specific body (monospaced command block, plan blurb, or plain title), optional detail and reason lines, and the trailing row of option buttons that resolve the request through ThreadRuntime.
key_symbols: ApprovalCard (struct View; let request: ApprovalRequest, let runtime: ThreadRuntime)
calls_into: ApprovalRequest (id, symbol, headline, kind, title, detail, reason, options) and its option type (Identifiable, role, title) from DroppyCode/Core/Models/Requests.swift
ApprovalRequest kind cases .command and .plan (all other kinds fall to default)
ThreadRuntime.resolve(_:option:) and ThreadRuntime.approvals (first element used for shortcut ownership)
side_effects: runtime.resolve(request, option: option) on any option button tap, which answers the approval request
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI .glassEffect(_:in:) plus .buttonStyle(.glass) / .buttonStyle(.glassProminent) (Liquid Glass styles, macOS 26 era SDK)
SF Symbol name supplied by request.symbol rendered with Image(systemName:)
Command-Return keyboard shortcut (KeyboardShortcut(.return, modifiers: .command)) as the approve chord
Design-family font .system(.callout, design: .monospaced) for command text
Hierarchical .quaternary shape style for the command block background
ui_elements: Root VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10), .padding(16)
Card background: .glassEffect(.regular.tint(Chrome.warning.opacity(0.1)), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous))
Header HStack(spacing: 8): Image(systemName: request.symbol).foregroundStyle(Chrome.warning) + Text(request.headline).font(.headline) + Spacer()

.command body: Text(request.title), font .system(.callout, design: .monospaced), textSelection(.enabled), lineLimit(8), padding 10, frame maxWidth .infinity alignment .leading, background .quaternary.opacity(0.5) in .rect(cornerRadius: 10, style: .continuous)
.plan body: literal text 'Approve the plan above to let the agent start building.', font .callout, foregroundStyle(.secondary)
default body: Text(request.title), font .callout, textSelection(.enabled)
detail line (when non-nil and non-empty): font .caption, .secondary, lineLimit(3)
reason line (when non-nil and non-empty): font .callout, .secondary
Button row: HStack(spacing: 8) with a leading Spacer, options iterated with request.options.reversed()
Approve-role option: .buttonStyle(.glassProminent) with Command-Return when the card owns the shortcut; other options: .buttonStyle(.glass)
feature_notes: Only the card whose request.id equals runtime.approvals.first?.id owns the Command-Return shortcut; other stacked cards pass nil so two cards never both claim the chord (the comment says two cards claiming it left neither reliably approving)
Options are drawn in reverse model order, so the last option in the model sits leftmost in the trailing-aligned row
Only .command gets the monospaced boxed treatment; .plan replaces the title entirely with the fixed sentence; every other kind shows the raw title as callout text
The card tint and the header symbol both use Chrome.warning (tint at opacity 0.1) so a theme recolours the whole card at once
Command text is selectable and clipped at 8 lines; the detail line is clipped at 3 lines; the reason line has no line limit
Both detail and reason are skipped when nil or empty, so the card collapses to headline plus body plus buttons
unresolved_questions: The full set of ApprovalRequest kind cases and the option role enum members besides .approve are defined in Core/Models/Requests.swift and were not read here
Whether request.symbol is always a valid SF Symbol name, and what headline/symbol defaults each kind uses, is decided in the model rather than this file
Chrome.warning's concrete colour value is in the UI/Chrome layer, not read here
The container that stacks several ApprovalCards and defines what 'top of the stack' means visually is outside this bundle

files.purpose: Defines ThreadChangesTab, the small glass tab that rises from the top edge of the chat box showing the thread's file-change summary (file count, additions, deletions) and, when clicked, opens the changes popover anchored to its own NSView.
side_effects: action() closure invoked on tap to open the changes popover
anchor(NSView) callback fired by AttachmentAnchorCapture in the background layer, handing the underlying NSView out so a popover can anchor to it
platform_assumptions: imports AppKit; the anchor closure traffics in NSView so an NSPopover can be anchored to this SwiftUI view
Uses the Unicode minus sign U+2212 rather than an ASCII hyphen for the deletions count
ui_elements: Shape: UnevenRoundedRectangle(topLeadingRadius: 12, topTrailingRadius: 12, style: .continuous) (bottom corners square, hidden under the composer)
Content HStack(spacing: 7)
Image(systemName: "plusminus") with Chrome.inlineIconFont, Chrome.secondaryText
File count text: '1 file' when stats.files.count == 1, otherwise '\(stats.files.count) files', in Chrome.primaryText.opacity(0.9)
Additions text: verbatim '+\(stats.additions)' in Chrome.success
Deletions text: verbatim '\u{2212}\(stats.deletions)' (Unicode minus) in Chrome.danger
Whole row font: .system(size: 12, weight: .medium).monospacedDigit()
Padding: .horizontal 12, .top 7, .bottom 7 + Self.overlap (7 + 14 = 21)
contentShape(shape), .buttonStyle(.plain), .focusable(false), .fixedSize()
Background material: .glassEffect(.regular.interactive(), in: shape)
Hidden background layer: AttachmentAnchorCapture(onResolve: anchor)
Tooltip: 'Show this thread's changes' concatenated with ShortcutStore.hint(for: .toggleChanges)
Accessibility label: '\(stats.files.count) files changed, \(stats.additions) added, \(stats.deletions) removed'
feature_notes: static overlap = 14 is the number of points the composer draws over the tab's lower edge, added as extra bottom padding so the visible tab height stays correct while the composer covers the bottom 14 points
The +/- hues deliberately match DiffStatLabel elsewhere in the app (Chrome.success / Chrome.danger) so a theme recolours the tab together with the diffs it stands for
Singular/plural is handled only for the file count; additions and deletions are always plain numbers with no pluralisation
The tab is not focusable, so keyboard focus traversal in the composer skips it
The keyboard shortcut for the same action is appended to the tooltip from ShortcutStore for the .toggleChanges action
Interactive glass is used, so the tab has a pressed/hover glass response rather than a custom highlight
unresolved_questions: FileChangeSummary.files element type and how additions/deletions are aggregated are defined in Core/Models/FileChangeSummary.swift, not read here
The exact format of ShortcutStore.hint(for:) output (leading space, parentheses, modifier glyphs) is in Core/Models/Shortcuts.swift, not read here
How AttachmentAnchorCapture resolves the NSView and when onResolve fires relative to layout is in UI/Common/AttachmentPreviewPanel.swift, not read here
The caller that supplies stats/anchor/action and positions the tab against the composer using Self.overlap is outside this bundle
